samples.summary: `assertValidBlock` is one level stricter than the writer it validates for: it 400s *any* block at depth 32, including the ordinary paragraphs inside the deepest legal table
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` increments `depth` once per table-cell descent (line 502: `assertValidBlock(cell.blocks[cb], ..., depth + 1)`), so `depth` is the number of enclosing tables — the same counter the readers keep. The new gate `if (depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH) throw` therefore rejects *every* block at depth 32, but the writer only refuses a **table** at depth >= 32 (`documentHasTableAtNestingCap`, packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231-241 checks `block.type === 'table'` before `depth >= MAX`). A table at depth 31 is legal for `writeDocsRoot` and is fully materialized by `treeNodeToBlock`, yet its cell's paragraph sits at depth 32 and is now a 400. Documents with exactly 32 nested tables are producible by the editor (`Doc.insertTableInCell` permits an insert while `tableNestingDepth(blockId) < 32`, i.e. a new table at depth 31) and by the DOCX importer (which the new test at packages/docs/test/import/docx-importer.test.ts asserts imports exactly `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` tables). Such a document cannot be saved through `PUT /content` — a GET→edit→PUT round trip fails with "blocks are nested too deeply". The correct gate is `depth > MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, or a gate on table blocks only.

samples.summary: `capTableNesting` returns unmodified blocks whenever `baseDepth <= 0`, so the "absolute nesting ceiling" it documents is never applied to a top-level paste
samples.evidence: `export function capTableNesting(blocks, baseDepth) { if (baseDepth <= 0) return blocks; ... }`. Every recursion and every drop decision is skipped for a fragment pasted at depth 0, so the function's stated invariant ("paste … owes the same absolute invariant" as the importer and CRDT writers) is enforced only for pastes into a cell. Today the only deep-nesting producer feeding `insertBlocks` is the sanitizer, which caps a fragment at `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (line 72/309), so nothing exceeds 32 in practice — but that makes the guard depend on an unrelated constant in another function rather than on its own condition, and any producer that later hands `insertBlocks` a deeper fragment bypasses the cap entirely. The same early-return also means `capTableCellsNesting(cells, 0)` (reachable if `Doc.tableNestingDepth` answers 0 from a stale parent map) is a no-op.
searchedFor: grep for callers of capTableNesting / capTableCellsNesting

samples.summary: The new paste/insert nesting guards read `Doc.tableNestingDepth`, which is backed by the layout-time `blockParentMap` and is documented to be stale for blocks created since the last layout — the cap then silently reads 0
samples.evidence: `insertBlocks` computes `this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId)` and `pasteTableCells` computes `this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) + (cellInfo ? 0 : 1)`. `tableNestingDepth` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:158-171) walks `this._blockParentMap` only, with no fallback walk — while `findBlockInCells` (same file, lines 325-331) explicitly documents that "the parent map is only rebuilt on layout, so a block created since the last layout — e.g. the tail block a paste splits out inside a cell — isn't in it yet". `insertBlocks` calls `ensureEditableBlock()` (which can split/create a block) immediately before reading the depth, exactly the situation the comment names. When the caret block is missing from the map the depth answers 0 and `capTableNesting` short-circuits, so a paste into a deeply nested cell is not capped at all.

samples.summary: `insertTable` takes the undo snapshot before the new nesting-cap early return, so a refused insert still pushes an undo checkpoint (and flushes presence) for a command that changed nothing
samples.evidence: `docStore.snapshot();` runs at line 4224, then the cell branch returns at line 4233 when `doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`. The comment on the guard says it is "Checked *before* the split so a refused insert leaves the document exactly as it was", but the snapshot has already been taken — for `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` that is an undo-stack/presence side effect on a no-op command. Moving the check above `docStore.snapshot()` would make the refusal fully inert.

finding.summary: New read-time truncation creates `tableData.rows === []` blocks that navigation code dereferences unguarded
finding.evidence: The change makes every reader materialize a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` as `{ ...tableData, rows: [] }` (crdt-tree.ts `treeNodeToBlock`: `depth >= MAX ? [] : ...`; yorkie-doc-store.ts line ~568 likewise). That block shape did not exist before this change. Multiple consumers assume a table block always has at least one row+cell+block: `text-editor.ts:4911` and `:4929` (`nextBlock.tableData.rows[0].cells[0].blocks[0].id` in `moveRight`), `:5142`, `:5177`, `:4743`, `:3223`. Arrow-navigating into a truncated table throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cells')`. `handleArrow` reportedly catches throws as "stale layout", but `moveRight`/`moveDown` are reached from other callers too. The truncation is deliberate; the unguarded consumers were never updated to expect it.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted evidence is largely wrong: moveLeft (text-editor.ts:4911-4953), moveRight (4955-4993), the arrow up/down block paths (3172-3181, 3200-3207, 3272-3279, 3300-3307) and moveVertical (5192-5207, 5235-5250) all route table entry through the new null-safe helpers firstCellBlock (77-81) / lastCellBlock (87-95) with `entered ?? block` fallbacks, and test/view/rowless-table-nav.test.ts covers the rowless-table arrow cases; lines 4743, 3223, 5142, 5177 are unrelated code. That alone would be `not-present`. But the same defect class does survive uncited in the same file: lastPositionInCell (3933-3941) does `const lastRow = td.rows[td.rows.length - 1]` then `lastRow.cells[...]` inside `while (lastBlock.type === 'table' && lastBlock.tableData)`, which throws TypeError on a truncated `rows: []` nested table, and it is called unguarded from Tab/Shift+Tab navigation at 5341, 5349, 6137 and 6146. Since a real, reachable instance of the claimed crash remains in this file's navigation code, I cannot refute the finding outright; it is kept, with the note that the actionable location is 3937 rather than the lines cited.

searchedFor: grep MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH across packages/frontend and packages/docs
finding.summary: `insertTableRow`/`insertTableColumn` still write rows/cells at or past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, creating exactly the "rows nobody can read" state the new refusal then makes permanent (the block becomes unwritable forever)
finding.evidence: `insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2933-2948) and `insertTableColumn` (2966-2990) build `buildRowNode(row, rowDepth)` / `buildCellNode(cells[r], rowDepth)` with no check that `rowDepth < MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, unlike `buildBlockNode` (386-402), which truncates at the cap, and unlike `Doc.insertTableInCell` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:925), which refuses. The PR's own test constructs the hazardous state with precisely this writer (`store.insertTableRow(atCap.id, 0, ...)` in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts's `peerRowsPastTheCap`). Once those rows exist, the new `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` makes every `updateBlock`/`updateTableCell` over the enclosing subtree throw (1833, 3021) — the subtree is permanently uneditable by every replica, not just refused once. Also note `insertTableRow` then splices the row into a model whose table read back as `rows: []`, so the local cache and any fresh read disagree immediately.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing depth check exists on both writers. `insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3007-3012) and `insertTableColumn` (3044-3049) both call `resolveTableRowDepth` and then `if (this.isPastReadableNesting(rowDepth)) { warnDeclinedTruncatedRowsWrite(...); return; }` before any `buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` call (3013, 3060) and before the local cache splice (3023, 3067-3069). The boundary is correct: `rowDepth = blockPathNestingDepth(path, region) + 1` (2936) and `isPastReadableNesting` returns `rowDepth > MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (2956-2957), i.e. it refuses exactly when the table block sits at depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH — the same depths `buildBlockNode` truncates (398-400) and `treeNodeToBlock` reports as `rows: []`. The finding's line citations (2933-2948, 2966-2990) point at the doc comments for `resolveTableRowDepth`/`isPastReadableNesting`, not the function bodies. Its test evidence is also contradicted: `peerRowsPastTheCap` (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3784-3822) deliberately writes the row via raw `doc.update(root.content.editByPath(...))` and comments that `insertTableRow` "now declines past the cap", with the pinning test at 3824. The secondary cache-divergence claim is unreachable for the same reason (the guard returns before the splice).
